answer: You may not use a personal laptop for work, except for a five-business-day IT continuity exception when your managed laptop is being repaired or replaced and you have no working device. IT must approve and log the exception before you use a personal machine, even for those five days. All other employees must use the managed laptop provided by NovaOps [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md § Personal laptops].

To reset MFA after replacing your phone, follow these steps from the IT knowledge base:

1. **Open a ticket** with the required fields: your employee ID, email, system (Okta), business impact, error text, and any safe screenshots. [documents/it_kb/mfa_reset.md § (whole document)]

2. **Verify identity** through a manager, HR, or IT video check to confirm it's you and there are no suspicious login attempts. [documents/it_kb/mfa_reset.md § (whole document)]

3. **Reset the MFA factor** in Okta Helpdesk — IT will handle this part after identity verification. [documents/it_kb/mfa_reset.md § (whole document)]

4. **Re-enroll immediately** with your new device once the reset is complete. [documents/it_kb/mfa_reset.md § (whole document)]

The [Okta Device Change KB](documents/it_kb/okta_device_change.md § (whole document)) also notes that if your new device isn't company-managed or approved BYOD, IT may need to check MDM enrollment and reset device trust before you can sign back into SSO apps.

The [Security and MFA Policy](documents/policies/security_and_mfa_policy.md § (whole document)) requires MFA on all accounts through Okta with no exceptions, and new devices always require identity verification even if you've already set up MFA elsewhere.
